Bus A returns at 15, 30, 45, … minutes. Write Bus B's list (20, 40, …) underneath and find the first shared time, then add it to 8:00.
onLevel.stemEs: Dos autobuses salen de la estación a las 8:00 AM. El autobús A regresa cada 15 minutos y el autobús B regresa cada 20 minutos. ¿Cuándo es la próxima vez que los dos autobuses están juntos en la estación?
onLevel.explanationEs: MCM(15, 20) = 60 minutos. Los dos autobuses regresan juntos 60 minutos después de las 8:00 AM, es decir, a las 9:00 AM.
hintsEs: Los dos autobuses salen juntos a las 8:00 y vuelven a coincidir después de una cantidad de minutos que 15 y 20 dividen exacto.
Escribe los minutos de regreso de cada autobús y busca el primer tiempo que aparezca en ambas listas; luego súmalo a las 8:00 AM.
El autobús A regresa a los 15, 30, 45, … minutos. Escribe abajo la lista del B (20, 40, …), halla el primer tiempo compartido y súmalo a las 8:00.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 6.12) Spot Maya's Mistake — LCM of 6 and 9

workedExample.label: Choose the answer
workedExample.work: Maya saw that 9 is bigger than 6, so she wrote LCM = 9.
workedExample.workEs: Maya vio que 9 es mayor que 6, así que escribió MCM = 9.

onLevel.correctWork: The LCM is not just the larger number. Check: 9 is in the multiples of 9, but it is NOT in the multiples of 6 (6, 12, 18...). The first number in BOTH lists is 18, so the LCM of 6 and 9 is 18.
hints: Maya picked 9 because it is the larger number. Is 9 a multiple of 6? Skip count: 6, 12, 18 — there is no 9.
The LCM must appear in BOTH multiple lists. Find the smallest number that is in the 6s AND the 9s: 18.
onLevel.titleEs: Encuentra el error de Maya — el m.c.m. de 6 y 9
onLevel.explanation: In the last step Maya chose 9 just because it is the larger number, but 9 never appears in the multiples of 6 (6, 12, 18, 24). The LCM has to be in both lists, and the first number in both is 18, so the LCM of 6 and 9 is 18.
onLevel.explanationEs: En el último paso Maya eligió 9 solo porque es el número mayor, pero 9 nunca aparece entre los múltiplos de 6 (6, 12, 18, 24). El m.c.m. tiene que estar en las dos listas, y el primer número que está en ambas es 18, así que el mínimo común múltiplo de 6 y 9 es 18.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El MCM no es simplemente el número mayor. Comprueba: 9 está en los múltiplos de 9, pero NO está en los múltiplos de 6 (6, 12, 18...). El primer número en AMBAS listas es 18, así que el MCM de 6 y 9 es 18.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 6.13) Two students found different factor trees for 60. Student A started with 2 × 30. Student B started with 6 × 10. Which statement is true?
choices: Both get the same prime factorization: 2 × 2 × 3 × 5
Only Student A gets the correct prime factorization
Only Student B gets the correct prime factorization
They will get different prime factorizations
onLevel.explanation: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic says every composite number has exactly one prime factorization. No matter how you start the factor tree, you always end with 2 × 2 × 3 × 5.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic says every composite number has exactly one prime factorization.
Starting with 6 × 10 is allowed, but so is starting with 2 × 30 — the opening pair does not decide who is right. Finish both trees and compare the primes at the ends.
Different starting pairs make the trees look different, but the primes at the very ends are what count. Finish both trees and list those primes before deciding.
hints: Notice the question isn't asking which START is right — it asks what happens when both finished trees are compared.
Finish BOTH trees yourself: keep splitting every branch down to primes, then compare the two final lists of prime factors.
Student A: 60 = 2 × 30, then 30 = 2 × 15, then 15 = 3 × 5. Now finish Student B's tree from 6 × 10 and compare the prime lists.
onLevel.stemEs: Dos estudiantes hicieron árboles de factores diferentes para 60. El estudiante A empezó con 2 × 30. El estudiante B empezó con 6 × 10. ¿Cuál afirmación es verdadera?
onLevel.explanationEs: El Teorema Fundamental de la Aritmética dice que todo número compuesto tiene exactamente una factorización prima. No importa cómo empieces el árbol de factores, siempre terminas con 2 × 2 × 3 × 5.
choicesEs: Los dos obtienen la misma factorización prima: 2 × 2 × 3 × 5
Solo el Estudiante A obtiene la factorización prima correcta
Solo el Estudiante B obtiene la factorización prima correcta
hintsEs: Fíjate que la pregunta no pregunta cuál INICIO es correcto — pregunta qué pasa cuando se comparan los dos árboles terminados.
Termina TÚ los DOS árboles: sigue partiendo cada rama hasta llegar a primos y luego compara las dos listas finales de factores primos.
Estudiante A: 60 = 2 × 30, luego 30 = 2 × 15, luego 15 = 3 × 5. Ahora termina el árbol del Estudiante B desde 6 × 10 y compara las listas de primos.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 6.13) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Find the prime factorization of 45, using exponents
workedExample.labelEs: Encuentra la factorización prima de 45, usando exponentes

onLevel.correctWork: 45 = 5 × 3 × 3 has one 5 and two 3's — not two 5's. The exponent on a prime factor shows how many times that factor appears, so the correct form is 45 = 3² × 5 (the 5 has no exponent shown because it appears only once).
hints: Count how many times each prime factor actually appears in the factor tree before you write its exponent.
5 only appears once in 45 = 3 × 3 × 5, so its exponent is 1 (usually left off) — not 2.
onLevel.explanation: An exponent records how many times a prime appears, and the last step gave the 5 an exponent of 2 even though 45 = 3 × 3 × 5 contains only one 5. Two 3s and one 5 means the correct form is 45 = 3² × 5.
onLevel.explanationEs: Un exponente indica cuántas veces aparece un factor primo, y el último paso le puso exponente 2 al 5 aunque 45 = 3 × 3 × 5 tiene un solo 5. Dos 3 y un 5 significan que la forma correcta es 45 = 3² × 5.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: 45 = 5 × 3 × 3 tiene un 5 y dos 3 — no dos 5. El exponente de un factor primo muestra cuántas veces aparece ese factor, así que la forma correcta es 45 = 3² × 5 (el 5 no lleva exponente porque aparece solo una vez).

onLevel.title: (Lesson 6.14) Spot the Common Mistake
onLevel.correctWork: 5(3x + 2) = 5 × 3x + 5 × 2 = 15x + 10. The student distributed the 5 to the 3x (getting 15x) but left the 2 unchanged. The factor must multiply every term inside, so 5 × 2 = 10, not 2.
hints: The 3x became 15x — what should happen to the 2 when you multiply by 5?
The distributive property says a(b + c) = ab + ac. The 5 must reach both 3x and 2.
onLevel.explanation: The 5 was distributed to the 3x, correctly giving 15x, but the 2 was copied down untouched. Both terms inside must be multiplied: 5(3x + 2) = 5 × 3x + 5 × 2 = 15x + 10, not 15x + 2.
onLevel.explanationEs: El 5 se distribuyó al 3x y dio correctamente 15x, pero el 2 se copió sin cambios. Los dos términos de adentro deben multiplicarse: 5(3x + 2) = 5 × 3x + 5 × 2 = 15x + 10, no 15x + 2.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: 5(3x + 2) = 5 × 3x + 5 × 2 = 15x + 10. El estudiante distribuyó el 5 al 3x (obteniendo 15x) pero dejó el 2 sin cambiar. El factor debe multiplicar cada término de adentro, así que 5 × 2 = 10, no 2.

onLevel.instructions: (Lesson 6.14) Use the distributive property to expand each expression.
hints: Some inside terms have coefficients, like 2x. Multiply the outside number by the WHOLE term: 3 × 2x.
Two products per row: outside × first term, outside × second term. Keep the − sign if the inside subtracts.
Row 1: 3(2x + 5) → 3 × 2x = 6x. Now multiply 3 × 5 and join the products with +. Repeat for each row.
onLevel.explanation: The outside factor multiplies the whole term inside, coefficient included, and the sign inside stays the same. So 3(2x + 5) = 6x + 15, 7(a − 4) = 7a − 28, 2(3m + 8) = 6m + 16, and 5(6 − y) = 30 − 5y.
onLevel.explanationEs: El factor de afuera multiplica el término completo de adentro, incluido su coeficiente, y el signo de adentro se mantiene igual. Así, 3(2x + 5) = 6x + 15, 7(a − 4) = 7a − 28, 2(3m + 8) = 6m + 16 y 5(6 − y) = 30 − 5y.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Usa la propiedad distributiva para desarrollar cada expresión.
hintsEs: Algunos términos de adentro tienen coeficiente, como 2x. Multiplica el número de afuera por el término COMPLETO: 3 × 2x.
Dos productos por fila: afuera × primer término y afuera × segundo término. Conserva el signo − si adentro hay resta.
Fila 1: 3(2x + 5) → 3 × 2x = 6x. Ahora multiplica 3 × 5 y une los productos con +. Repite en cada fila.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 6.15) Spot the Mistake — Swept-Up Constant
onLevel.correctWork: The 4 is a constant with no variable, so it cannot be combined with the x-terms. Combine only the like terms: 6x + 2x = 8x, and the 4 stays on its own. The correct simplified expression is 8x + 4. (Check: at x = 1, 6x + 4 + 2x = 6 + 4 + 2 = 12, and 8x + 4 = 12, but 12x = 12 only by accident — at x = 2 it gives 24 instead of the true 20.)
hints: Is 4 a like term with 6x and 2x? It has no variable, so it cannot join them.
Combine the x-terms first (6x + 2x = 8x), then write the leftover constant: 8x + 4.
onLevel.titleEs: Descubre el error — la constante arrastrada
onLevel.explanation: The Combine step swept the constant 4 in with the coefficients 6 and 2, but 4 has no variable, so it is not a like term. Only 6x + 2x = 8x combine, and the 4 stays on its own, giving 8x + 4 — at x = 2 that is 20, while 12x would give 24.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de combinar arrastró la constante 4 junto con los coeficientes 6 y 2, pero el 4 no tiene variable, así que no es un término semejante. Solo se combinan 6x + 2x = 8x, y el 4 se queda aparte, lo que da 8x + 4; con x = 2 eso es 20, mientras que 12x daría 24.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El 4 es una constante sin variable, así que no puede combinarse con los términos con x. Combina solo los términos semejantes: 6x + 2x = 8x, y el 4 se queda solo. La expresión simplificada correcta es 8x + 4. (Comprueba: en x = 1, 6x + 4 + 2x = 6 + 4 + 2 = 12, y 8x + 4 = 12, pero 12x = 12 solo por casualidad — en x = 2 da 24 en lugar del verdadero 20.)

onLevel.instructions: (Lesson 6.15) Simplify each expression by combining like terms.
hints: Row 1 shows the move: gather the matching variable terms first, then bring the constant along.
For each row, underline the variable terms and circle the constants. Combine each group separately.
Row 2: 6x + 4 + 2x + 7 — pair 6x with 2x, and 4 with 7. Add each pair, then write both parts.
onLevel.explanation: In each row you combine the variable terms and the constants separately: 3a + 5a = 8a leaves 8a + 2; 6x + 2x = 8x with 4 + 7 = 11 gives 8x + 11; 10m − 3m = 7m gives 7m + 5; and 4y + y = 5y with 3 + 9 = 12 gives 5y + 12. The constants never merge with the variable terms because they have no variable.
onLevel.explanationEs: En cada fila combinas por separado los términos con variable y las constantes: 3a + 5a = 8a deja 8a + 2; 6x + 2x = 8x con 4 + 7 = 11 da 8x + 11; 10m − 3m = 7m da 7m + 5; y 4y + y = 5y con 3 + 9 = 12 da 5y + 12. Las constantes nunca se unen con los términos con variable porque no tienen variable.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Simplifica cada expresión combinando los términos semejantes.
hintsEs: La fila 1 muestra el movimiento: junta primero los términos con la misma variable y luego lleva la constante.
Para cada fila, subraya los términos con variable y encierra las constantes. Combina cada grupo por separado.
Fila 2: 6x + 4 + 2x + 7 — junta 6x con 2x, y 4 con 7. Suma cada pareja y luego escribe ambas partes.

extending.title: (Lesson 6.4) Find the Evaluation Error
extending.correctWork: 4(2²) + 3 = 4(4) + 3 = 16 + 3 = 19. Square the 2 first, THEN multiply by 4.
hints: Order of operations: what should happen first — squaring the 2, or multiplying 4 × 2?
The exponent applies only to x, not to 4x. Evaluate 2² = 4 first, then multiply by 4.
extending.explanation: The exponent in 4x² belongs only to x, not to 4x, so the work cannot be rewritten as (4 × 2)². Square first: 2² = 4, then multiply by 4 to get 16, then add 3 for 19. Treating it as 8² inflated the answer all the way to 67.
extending.explanationEs: El exponente en 4x² pertenece solo a x, no a 4x, así que el trabajo no se puede reescribir como (4 × 2)². Primero se eleva al cuadrado: 2² = 4, luego se multiplica por 4 para obtener 16 y después se suma 3 para llegar a 19. Tratarlo como 8² infló la respuesta hasta 67.
extending.correctWorkEs: 4(2²) + 3 = 4(4) + 3 = 16 + 3 = 19. Eleva el 2 al cuadrado primero, y DESPUÉS multiplica por 4.

extending.title: (Lesson 6.5) Find the Translation Error

workedExample.label: Reasoning
workedExample.work: I see 'less than' so I subtract, and 12 comes first in the phrase.
workedExample.workEs: Veo 'menos que' así que resto, y el 12 aparece primero en la frase.

extending.correctWork: '12 less than a number g' means start with g and subtract 12: g − 12. The phrase 'less than' reverses the order — the number being subtracted FROM comes after 'less than.'
hints: Does '12 less than g' mean start with 12 or start with g?
Try it with numbers: '5 less than 20' means 20 − 5 = 15, not 5 − 20.
extending.explanation: The expression step copied the numbers in the order they appear, but "less than" reverses them. "12 less than a number g" starts at g and takes 12 away, so it is g − 12 — the same way "5 less than 20" means 20 − 5 = 15.
extending.explanationEs: El paso de la expresión copió los números en el orden en que aparecen, pero "menos que" los invierte. "12 menos que un número g" empieza en g y le quita 12, así que es g − 12, igual que "5 menos que 20" significa 20 − 5 = 15.
extending.correctWorkEs: '12 menos que un número g' significa empezar con g y restar 12: g − 12. La frase 'menos que' invierte el orden — el número al que se le resta viene después de 'menos que'.

extending.title: (Lesson 6.6) Find the Simplification Error
extending.correctWork: 3x + 2x = 5x (NOT 5x²). When you combine like terms, you add the coefficients, not multiply them. The correct answer is 5x + 6.
hints: When you combine 3x + 2x, do you add the exponents or the coefficients?
3x means 3 groups of x. 2x means 2 groups of x. Together that's ___ groups of x.
extending.explanation: Rearranging to 3x + 2x + 5 + 1 is correct. The error is in the last step: combining like terms adds the COEFFICIENTS, so 3x + 2x = 5x, not 5x². The exponent never changes when you add like terms, so the answer is 5x + 6.
extending.explanationEs: Reacomodar a 3x + 2x + 5 + 1 está correcto. El error está en el último paso: combinar términos semejantes suma los COEFICIENTES, así que 3x + 2x = 5x, no 5x². El exponente no cambia nunca al sumar términos semejantes, así que la respuesta es 5x + 6.
extending.correctWorkEs: 3x + 2x = 5x (NO 5x²). Al combinar términos semejantes, sumas los coeficientes, no los multiplicas. La respuesta correcta es 5x + 6.

extending.title: (Lesson 6.7) Find Amara's Mistake

workedExample.label: List common factors
workedExample.labelEs: Haz la lista de factores comunes

extending.correctWork: GCF = 4 (the greatest of the common factors, not just any common factor). Amara found the common factors correctly but chose 2 instead of the largest one, 4.
hints: Amara found the common factors correctly. Look at Step 4 — did she pick the greatest one?
The GCF is the LARGEST common factor. Look at the list: 1, 2, 4. Which is biggest?
extending.explanation: Amara's factor lists and her list of common factors (1, 2, 4) are all correct. The error is in the last step: she chose 2, but the GCF has to be the greatest of the shared factors, which is 4. So the GCF of 16 and 28 is 4, not 2.
extending.explanationEs: Las listas de factores de Amara y su lista de factores comunes (1, 2, 4) están correctas. El error está en el último paso: eligió 2, pero el MCD tiene que ser el mayor de los factores compartidos, que es 4. Entonces el MCD de 16 y 28 es 4, no 2.
extending.correctWorkEs: MCD = 4 (el mayor de los factores comunes, no cualquier factor común). Amara encontró bien los factores comunes, pero eligió 2 en lugar del más grande, 4.

extending.title: (Lesson 6.8) Find the Property Error

workedExample.label: Student's claim
workedExample.work: This shows the Commutative Property of Subtraction.
workedExample.workEs: Esto muestra la Propiedad Conmutativa de la Resta.

workedExample.label: Reasoning
workedExample.work: I switched the order, so it must be commutative.
workedExample.workEs: Cambié el orden, así que debe ser conmutativa.

extending.correctWork: 15 − 8 = 7, but 8 − 15 = −7. These are NOT equal. The commutative property does NOT apply to subtraction. It only works for addition and multiplication.
hints: Does switching the order in subtraction always give the same answer?
Try computing both sides: Is 15 − 8 the same as 8 − 15?
extending.explanation: The claim fails as soon as you compute: 15 − 8 = 7 but 8 − 15 = −7, so the two sides are not equal and no property is being shown. The commutative property applies only to addition and multiplication, never to subtraction or division.
extending.explanationEs: La afirmación falla en cuanto calculas: 15 − 8 = 7 pero 8 − 15 = −7, así que los dos lados no son iguales y no se muestra ninguna propiedad. La propiedad conmutativa aplica solo a la suma y la multiplicación, nunca a la resta ni a la división.
extending.correctWorkEs: 15 − 8 = 7, pero 8 − 15 = −7. NO son iguales. La propiedad conmutativa NO aplica a la resta. Solo funciona para la suma y la multiplicación.

extending.title: (Lesson 6.9) Find the Division Error
extending.correctWork: 6 × 3/2 (flip the divisor 2/3 to get 3/2, not keep it as 2/3). Then 6 × 3/2 = 18/2 = 9.
hints: In 'Keep, Change, Flip' — which fraction gets flipped?
The divisor (2/3) should become its reciprocal (3/2). Did Step 2 flip the right fraction?
extending.explanation: The Keep, Change, Flip step kept the divisor as 2/3 instead of flipping it to its reciprocal 3/2. The correct work is 6 × 3/2 = 18/2 = 9. Nine also makes sense as a count: each whole holds one and a half 2/3-size pieces, so 6 wholes hold 9 of them — more than the 6 you started with, not less.
extending.explanationEs: En el paso de Conservar, Cambiar, Invertir se dejó el divisor como 2/3 en vez de invertirlo a su recíproco 3/2. El trabajo correcto es 6 × 3/2 = 18/2 = 9. El 9 también tiene sentido como conteo: cada entero contiene una pieza y media de 2/3, así que 6 enteros contienen 9 de ellas, más que el 6 inicial, no menos.
extending.correctWorkEs: 6 × 3/2 (voltea el divisor 2/3 para obtener 3/2, no lo dejes como 2/3). Entonces 6 × 3/2 = 18/2 = 9.

extending.title: (Lesson 6.10) Find the Mixed Number Error
extending.correctWork: 2 1/3 = 7/3 (not 6/3). Multiply: 2 × 3 = 6, then ADD the numerator 1 to get 7. So 7/3 × 2/1 = 14/3 = 4 2/3.
hints: Check the conversion: 2 × 3 = 6, then add the numerator 1 to get 7.
2 1/3 should convert to 7/3, not 6/3. The student forgot to add the numerator.
extending.titleEs: Encuentra el error del número mixto
extending.explanation: The Convert step is wrong: the student wrote 2 1/3 = 6/3, multiplying 2 × 3 but never adding the numerator. The correct conversion is (2 × 3 + 1)/3 = 7/3, so 7/3 × 2/1 = 14/3 = 4 2/3.
extending.explanationEs: El paso Convertir está mal: el estudiante escribió 2 1/3 = 6/3, multiplicando 2 × 3 pero sin sumar nunca el numerador. La conversión correcta es (2 × 3 + 1)/3 = 7/3, así que 7/3 × 2/1 = 14/3 = 4 2/3.
extending.correctWorkEs: 2 1/3 = 7/3 (no 6/3). Multiplica: 2 × 3 = 6, y luego SUMA el numerador 1 para obtener 7. Así que 7/3 × 2/1 = 14/3 = 4 2/3.

extending.title: (Lesson 6.11) Find the Problem-Solving Error

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: A tank has 3/4 gallon of water. Each bucket holds 1/6 gallon. How many buckets can be filled?
workedExample.workEs: Un tanque tiene 3/4 de galón de agua. Cada cubeta contiene 1/6 de galón. ¿Cuántas cubetas se pueden llenar?

extending.correctWork: The equation should be 3/4 ÷ 1/6 (total ÷ group size). Then 3/4 × 6/1 = 18/4 = 4 1/2 buckets.
hints: Which value is the total being divided — 3/4 or 1/6?
The student wrote the dividend and divisor in the wrong order. The total (3/4) should come first.
extending.titleEs: Encuentra el error al resolver el problema
extending.explanation: The dividend and divisor are swapped. The 3/4 gallon is the total being split up and 1/6 gallon is one bucket, so the equation must be 3/4 ÷ 1/6 = 3/4 × 6/1 = 18/4 = 4 1/2 buckets. An answer of 2/9 of a bucket is a warning sign, since a 1/6-gallon bucket clearly fits inside 3/4 gallon more than once.
extending.explanationEs: El dividendo y el divisor están invertidos. Los 3/4 de galón son el total que se reparte y 1/6 de galón es una cubeta, así que la ecuación debe ser 3/4 ÷ 1/6 = 3/4 × 6/1 = 18/4 = 4 1/2 cubetas. Una respuesta de 2/9 de cubeta es una señal de alerta, porque una cubeta de 1/6 de galón claramente cabe más de una vez dentro de 3/4 de galón.
extending.correctWorkEs: La ecuación debe ser 3/4 ÷ 1/6 (total ÷ tamaño del grupo). Entonces 3/4 × 6/1 = 18/4 = 4 1/2 cubetas.

extending.title: (Lesson 6.12) Find Jaylen's Mistake

workedExample.label: Find LCM of 8 and 12
workedExample.workEs: Haz la lista de múltiplos de 8 y de 12

extending.correctWork: LCM = 24 (the least common multiple is the SMALLEST shared multiple, not just any common multiple)
hints: Jaylen correctly listed the common multiples. Look at Step 5 — did he pick the smallest one?
The LCM is the LEAST (smallest) common multiple. 24 and 48 are both common multiples, but which is smaller?
extending.explanation: Jaylen listed the common multiples 24 and 48 correctly, but in the final step he chose 48 instead of the smaller one. LEAST common multiple means the smallest shared multiple, so the answer is 24.
extending.explanationEs: Jaylen escribió correctamente los múltiplos comunes 24 y 48, pero en el paso final eligió 48 en lugar del menor. Mínimo común múltiplo significa el múltiplo compartido más pequeño, así que la respuesta es 24.
extending.correctWorkEs: MCM = 24 (el mínimo común múltiplo es el múltiplo compartido MÁS PEQUEÑO, no cualquier múltiplo común)

extending.title: (Lesson 6.13) Find Marcus's Mistake
extending.correctWork: 8 = 2 × 4, but 4 is not prime. 4 = 2 × 2, so 8 = 2 × 2 × 2. The correct prime factorization is 48 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 2⁴ × 3.
hints: Look at Step 4 — is every factor in the answer a prime number?
4 is not prime because 4 = 2 × 2. Marcus needed to keep breaking it down.
extending.explanation: Marcus stopped the 8 branch while a composite factor was still in it: 4 is not prime because 4 = 2 × 2, so 8 = 2 × 2 × 2, not 2 × 4. Finishing that branch gives 48 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 2⁴ × 3.
extending.explanationEs: Marcus detuvo la rama del 8 cuando todavía tenía un factor compuesto: 4 no es primo porque 4 = 2 × 2, así que 8 = 2 × 2 × 2, no 2 × 4. Al terminar esa rama se obtiene 48 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 2⁴ × 3.
extending.correctWorkEs: 8 = 2 × 4, pero 4 no es primo. 4 = 2 × 2, así que 8 = 2 × 2 × 2. La factorización prima correcta es 48 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 2⁴ × 3.

extending.title: (Lesson 6.14) Find the Distributive Error
extending.correctWork: 5(2x + 4) = 5 × 2x + 5 × 4 = 10x + 20. You must distribute the 5 to BOTH terms inside the parentheses, not just the first one.
hints: Did the student multiply 5 by both terms, or only the first term?
The distributive property says a(b + c) = ab + ac. Both b and c get multiplied.
extending.titleEs: Encuentra el error de la propiedad distributiva
extending.explanation: The 5 multiplied only the first term inside. Distributing to both gives 5(2x + 4) = 5 × 2x + 5 × 4 = 10x + 20. Testing with x = 1 confirms it: the original 5(2 + 4) = 30 and 10(1) + 20 = 30, while the student's 10x + 4 would give only 14.
extending.explanationEs: El 5 multiplicó solo el primer término de adentro. Al distribuir a los dos: 5(2x + 4) = 5 × 2x + 5 × 4 = 10x + 20. Probar con x = 1 lo confirma: la expresión original 5(2 + 4) = 30 y 10(1) + 20 = 30, mientras que el 10x + 4 del estudiante daría apenas 14.
extending.correctWorkEs: 5(2x + 4) = 5 × 2x + 5 × 4 = 10x + 20. Debes distribuir el 5 a AMBOS términos dentro del paréntesis, no solo al primero.

extending.title: (Lesson 6.15) Find the Simplification Error
extending.correctWork: 5x + 4x = 9x (like terms). 2y stays separate (no other y-term). The constant 3 stays. Correct answer: 9x + 2y + 3. You cannot combine x-terms and y-terms into xy.
hints: Can you combine 5x and 2y? Do they have the same variable?
Like terms must have the exact same variable. 5x and 4x are like terms, but 5x and 2y are not.
extending.explanation: The Simplify step merged the x-terms and the y-term into 11xy, but terms with different variables can never be combined. Only 5x + 4x = 9x are like terms; 2y and the constant 3 each stand alone, so the expression simplifies to 9x + 2y + 3.
extending.explanationEs: El paso de simplificar juntó los términos con x y el término con y en 11xy, pero los términos con variables distintas nunca se pueden combinar. Solo 5x + 4x = 9x son términos semejantes; 2y y la constante 3 quedan cada uno por su lado, así que la expresión se simplifica a 9x + 2y + 3.
extending.correctWorkEs: 5x + 4x = 9x (términos semejantes). 2y se queda aparte (no hay otro término con y). La constante 3 se queda. Respuesta correcta: 9x + 2y + 3. No puedes combinar términos con x y términos con y en xy.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Simplify Algebraic Expressions is sweeping a constant into the variable terms — for example, simplifying 6x + 4 + 2x as 12x by adding all three numbers (6 + 4 + 2 = 12) instead of recognizing that 4 has no variable and cannot combine with 6x and 2x. The correct simplified expression is 8x + 4 (combine 6x + 2x = 8x, and let the 4 stay on its own). Before you submit, check that every term you combined has the exact same variable part.

diagram.title: Combining the Festival Cable Order
diagram.caption: Each row holds one type of term: add the m-parts (8+3+4=15m) and the number-parts (5+7+2=14) separately to get 15m + 14.

connect.scenario: A music festival needs supplies for 3 stages. Stage 1 needs 8m + 5 cables, Stage 2 needs 3m + 7 cables, and Stage 3 needs 4m + 2 cables, where m represents the number of microphones per stage. The total order is (8m + 5) + (3m + 7) + (4m + 2).
connect.promptQuestion: Simplify the total order expression. What does each part of the simplified expression tell you?
connect.prompt: The total order simplifies to ___m + ___. The ___ tells us ___ and the ___ tells us ___.

check.explanation: Add the m-terms: 8m + 3m + 4m = 15m. Add the constants: 5 + 7 + 2 = 14. 15m and 14 are unlike terms, so they cannot be combined.

check.stem: What does the 15m tell the festival?
choices: 15 cables are needed for every microphone
check.explanation: 15 is the coefficient of m, so for each microphone the festival needs 15 cables across all three stages.

check.stem: If each stage has 4 microphones (m = 4), how many cables in total?

connect.modelAnswer: (8m + 5) + (3m + 7) + (4m + 2) = 15m + 14. The 15m says 15 cables are needed for every microphone, and the 14 is the fixed number of extra cables needed no matter how many microphones there are. With m = 4, that is 15(4) + 14 = 74 cables.
